promise a credit or amount. The team voice file signs off with "Warmly," followed by

graders.evidence:
Ticket 1017 is outside the refund window, so the draft below doesn't promise a refund. Taylor was charged on 2026-08-20 and wrote in on 2026-09-29, which is **40 days** later (the plugin's date script calculated this). Refund policy kb-101 only allows full refunds within 14 days. After that, only a support lead can review the account and offer a credit. The draft offers that review instead.

---

**Draft - internal note, not sent** (ticket 1017, billing, language en)

> Hi Taylor,
>
> Thanks for letting us know you haven't been getting much use out of Quillfern since your renewal. I can see why paying $588.00 for that feels frustrating.
>
> Here's where things stand. A full refund is available within 14 days of the charge date. Your annual renewal was charged on 2026-08-20, so it's outside that window and can't be refunded the standard way.
>
> What I can do is ask a support lead to review your account. In exceptional cases they can offer an account credit. If you'd like that review, the account owner just needs to reply to this ticket, and the support lead will answer within 2 business days.
>
> You can read more in our help article "Refunds and billing credits."
>
> Warmly,
> Morgan at Quillfern Support

---
**Sources:** kb-101 "Refunds and billing credits". Macro m-201 doesn't apply because it covers refunds within the 14-day window.

**Claims:**
- Full refunds are available within 14 days of the charge date [KB kb-101]
- The renewal on 2026-08-20 is outside the 14-day window [KB kb-101; computed as 40 days]
- A support lead can review the account and may offer a credit in exceptional cases [KB kb-101]
- The account owner replies to the ticket to request a review, and the lead answers within 2 business days [KB kb-101]
- $588.00 and 2026-08-20 come from the customer's own message [ASSUMED - check against the billing record]

**Before sending:**
- Check in billing that the charge was $588.00 on 2026-08-20. If it was a duplicate or a billing error, kb-101 says it is always refunded, so reply with the refund wording instead.
- The ticket has **churn** and **repeat** flags. Ticket 1008 (same customer, closed 2026-09-23) was about being charged twice for September. Morgan's reply on 1008 only said it was "resolved on our side", so confirm that duplicate really was refunded. Consider sending this ticket to the support lead now for a credit review rather than waiting for the customer to ask.
- Check whether Taylor is the account owner, since only the owner can request the review.
- The SLA is due 2026-10-03 10:05 UTC, about 25 hours from now.

Copy it into the ticket yourself, or, if your helpdesk connector is connected, I can add it as an internal note after you confirm.

# Support week 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-02
*As of 2026-10-02T09:00Z (the sample's snapshot time). Source: the sample Freshdesk CSV export, 40 tickets. 1 blank row was skipped.*

**Headline:** We got 30 new tickets this week, up from 10 last week (+200%). Billing was the biggest driver, and every booking-form and timezone ticket we answered had to be worked from scratch because there's no macro or help article for either topic.

| Metric | This window | Prior window |
|---|---|---|
| Tickets created | 30 | 10 |
| SLA misses | 2 (1018, 1024) | 2 (1005, 1011) |
| CSAT good share | 81.8% (9/11) | - |
| Open right now | 16 | - |

## Top 3 drivers
1. **Billing: 5 tickets (prior 2).** Invoice name changes, prorated upgrades, missing receipts, a refund request for a $588.00 renewal (1017), and an urgent VIP complaint about being charged and then downgraded (1026).
2. **Access: 4 tickets (prior 1).** A password reset email that never arrived, a lockout, a 2FA reset for a former manager, and an alert about a login from an unknown country (1040, flagged as security).
3. **Booking form: 4 tickets (prior 1).** All four ask how to add custom or required questions (allergies, first visit only, student name, parents' school).

## Detractors
- **1018 (timezone):** "no comment". SMS reminders went out an hour early after the daylight saving change, and the same customer wrote in again as 1039. Follow-up: one Tier 2 owner should call the customer and close out 1018 and 1039 together.
- **1031 (booking-form):** "no comment". The customer asked how to add a required "student name" question. Follow-up: send the steps once the macro below exists, and ask what was missing from our answer.
- *Note: CSV exports don't include the reply thread, so "no comment" may just mean the comment wasn't exported. Check the comments in Freshdesk.*

## Macros to write
- **Booking form (4 tickets: 1015, 1022, 1031, 1032): "Adding custom questions to your booking form"**
  - How to add a question, mark it as required, and limit it to first visits only. Include examples: allergies, student name, parent details.
  - No help article covers this yet, so every step is [ASSUMED - check with product].
- **Data export (3 tickets: 1012, 1013, 1019): "Exporting bookings, clients and prices"**
  - Owners and admins go to Reports > Export. Each export covers up to 12 months, and the download link is emailed and valid for 24 hours [KB-104].

- **Timezone (3 tickets: 1018, 1024, 1039): "Reminder or booking times off by an hour"**
  - Check that the business time zone and each staff member's calendar time zone match [KB-103, step 3].
  - Explain how the booking page shows slots to clients in other time zones, and how daylight saving is handled: [ASSUMED - check with product].

## KB articles to write

  - Showing a question only on a client's first visit
  - Where answers appear on the booking and client record
- **Timezone (3 tickets): "Time zones, daylight saving and reminders"**
  - How the business, staff and client time zones interact
  - How client-facing booking slots are shown across time zones [ASSUMED]
  - What happens to reminder times at a daylight saving change, and what to check [ASSUMED]

Ticket 1012 (export missing prices, needed for payroll today) is unassigned and breaches its SLA in 3h15m. Ticket 1028 is solved, so its 10 minutes to the SLA due time doesn't matter.
